**PICO.**
Population, intervention, comparator and outcomes. It fixes the question an
assessment answers, and in the EU joint clinical assessment each member state
can ask for its own PICO.

**Relative effectiveness.**
How well a treatment works compared with the alternatives used for the same
patients in practice. It is the core question of an HTA, while a marketing
authorisation can rest on efficacy against placebo.

**Joint clinical assessment.**
The EU-wide assessment of relative clinical effectiveness under Regulation
(EU) 2021/2282, applied since January 2025 to new cancer medicines and
advanced therapy medicinal products. It reports the size of each effect and
the certainty of the evidence, and it leaves the judgement of value to the
member states.

**Added benefit.**
In the German AMNOG process, the extent to which a new medicine improves
patient-relevant outcomes over the appropriate comparator therapy set by the
Federal Joint Committee (G-BA). IQWiG assesses the evidence, the G-BA decides
the extent of added benefit, and the price negotiation starts from that
decision.

**Anchored and unanchored comparison.**
An anchored comparison links two treatments through a comparator arm that
both trials share, so each trial keeps its randomisation. An unanchored
comparison has no shared arm, for example two single-arm studies, and is only
valid if every prognostic factor and effect modifier has been adjusted for.

**Effect modifier.**
A patient characteristic that changes the relative effect of a treatment, for
example a hazard ratio that differs by disease stage. If effect modifiers are
distributed differently across trials, an indirect comparison is biased, even
when it is anchored.

**Prognostic factor.**
A characteristic that predicts the outcome whatever the treatment, for example
age for mortality. It does not bias an anchored comparison on the relative
scale, but it does bias an unanchored one unless it is adjusted for.

**Transitivity.**
The assumption that the trials in a network are similar enough that any
patient could, in principle, have been randomised to any of the treatments.
In practice it means that effect modifiers are distributed alike across the
comparisons.

**Consistency.**
Agreement between the direct and the indirect evidence on the same
comparison. It can be tested only where a closed loop of trials exists, and
passing the test does not prove transitivity.

**Estimand.**
A precise statement of the treatment effect a study targets: population,
treatments, endpoint, handling of intercurrent events and population-level
summary (ICH E9(R1)). It fixes what question a number answers before anyone
chooses how to estimate it.
